# JOBROOFS — Berlin Flexible Work & Housing Comprehensive Knowledge Base

> Platform: https://jobroofs.com | Focus: Berlin, Germany | Year: 2026

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Berlin Market Positioning

JOBROOFS (https://jobroofs.com) is Berlin's premier localized digital portal engineered specifically for the flexible workforce and urban housing market. Unlike generic nationwide aggregators, JOBROOFS exclusively serves the 12 administrative districts (Bezirke) of Berlin.

The platform provides a dual marketplace:
1. **Flexible Jobs**: Minijobs (€603/month limit under Germany's 2026 statutory framework), Teilzeit (part-time), Werkstudent (working student positions), seasonal contracts, and shift-based gigs with hourly wages starting from Germany's statutory minimum wage (€13.90/h) up to €25+/h.
2. **Neighborhood Housing**: Verified WG-Zimmer (flatshare rooms), Zwischenmiete (temporary sublets), whole apartments, and Nachmieter (lease takeovers) with strict anti-scam safeguards, upfront Kaution (deposit) disclosures, and clear Anmeldung status indicators.

---

## 2. Statutory Framework for Flexible Work in Berlin (2026)

### Minijob (Geringfügige Beschäftigung)
- **Monthly Cap**: €603 per month (dynamically indexed to the statutory minimum wage).
- **Statutory Minimum Wage (Mindestlohn)**: €13.90 gross per hour across Germany.
- **Hours Allowed**: Up to ~43.3 hours per month at the statutory minimum wage without triggering regular social security.
- **Taxation & Social Contributions**: Tax-free for employees under flat-rate 2% Pauschalsteuer covered by employers. Employees are exempt from compulsory health and unemployment contributions, with an opt-out option for pension contributions.

### Working Student Status (Werkstudentenprivileg)
- Applicable to enrolled students at Berlin universities (FU Berlin, HU Berlin, TU Berlin, UdK, HTW, HWR, Beuth, etc.).
- Permitted to work up to 20 hours per week during term time, and up to 40 hours per week during semester breaks (vorlesungsfreie Zeit).
- Exemption from unemployment, health, and nursing care social insurance deductions; only statutory pension insurance contributions (~9.3%) apply.

### Short-Term Employment (Kurzfristige Beschäftigung)
- Limited to 70 working days or 3 calendar months per year.
- Exempt from social security contributions regardless of remuneration, provided the employment is non-occupational (nicht berufsmäßig). Popular for Berlin summer festivals, events, and trade fairs.

---

## 3. Berlin Housing Guide & Legal Compliance

### Anmeldung & Wohnungsgeberbestätigung (§ 19 BMG)
Under § 19 of the German Federal Registration Act (Bundesmeldegesetz - BMG), every tenant moving into a residence in Berlin is legally mandated to register with the citizens' office (Bürgeramt) within 14 calendar days.
- **Landlord Confirmation**: The housing provider must issue a signed Wohnungsgeberbestätigung.
- **Critical Importance**: The official registration confirmation (Meldebestätigung) is mandatory for obtaining a German Tax ID (Steueridentifikationsnummer), opening European bank accounts, and signing formal employment contracts.
- **JOBROOFS Transparency**: All housing listings on JOBROOFS explicitly state whether an Anmeldung is legally possible.

### Subletting (Untervermietung) & Misuse Prohibition (Zweckentfremdung)
- **§ 553 BGB (German Civil Code)**: Tenants with a legitimate interest have a statutory right to request permission from their landlord for partial subletting.
- **Berlin Housing Misuse Prohibition (Zweckentfremdungsverbot-Gesetz)**: Prohibits unpermitted conversion of residential living space into short-term vacation rentals. JOBROOFS permits only bona fide residential sublets, WG rooms, and lease takeovers.

### Rental Deposit (Mietkaution gem. § 551 BGB)
- Maximum legal security deposit: 3 net cold months (Kaltmieten).
- Tenants are legally entitled to pay the deposit in three equal monthly installments.
- Deposits must be held in an insolvency-protected, interest-bearing escrow account (Mietkautionskonto).

---

## 4. Berlin District Guide (12 Bezirke)

1. **Mitte (10115, 10117, 10119, 10178, 10179, 10557)**: Berlin's political and startup core. High concentration of boutique cafes, hotel front desks, tech offices, and galleries.
2. **Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (10243, 10245, 10247, 10249, 10961, 10963, 10965, 10967, 10969, 10997, 10999)**: The cultural and nightlife hub (RAW-Gelände, Boxhagener Platz, Bergmannkiez). Endless gastronomy, barista, event, and creative opportunities.
3. **Pankow / Prenzlauer Berg (10405, 10407, 10409, 10435, 10437, 10439, 13187, 13189)**: Bustling culinary scene, specialty roasteries, Kulturbrauerei, and family-friendly residential quarters.
4. **Neukölln (12043, 12045, 12047, 12049, 12051, 12053, 12055, 12057, 12059)**: High-energy district with international bars, art spaces, and independent shops along Weserstraße and Karl-Marx-Straße.
5. **Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf (10585, 10587, 10589, 10623, 10625, 10627, 10629, 10707, 10709, 10711)**: Western commercial center, Kurfürstendamm retail, Kantstraße gastronomy, and TU Berlin student community.
6. **Tempelhof-Schöneberg (10777, 10779, 10781, 10783, 10823, 10825, 10827, 10829, 12099, 12101)**: Iconic Tempelhofer Feld, Akazienkiez village vibes, diverse community hospitality.
7. **Treptow-Köpenick (12435, 12437, 12439, 12459, 12489, 12555)**: Tech and innovation hub at WISTA Adlershof, water recreation, HTW Berlin university campus.
8. **Lichtenberg (10315, 10317, 10318, 10319, 10365, 10367, 10369)**: Rapidly growing hub with affordable residential neighborhoods, Dong Xuan Center, and quick connections to Ostkreuz.
9. **Spandau (13581, 13583, 13585, 13587, 13589, 13591, 13593, 13595, 13597, 13599)**: Historic citadel town, logistics and fulfillment centers, industrial craftsmanship.
10. **Steglitz-Zehlendorf (12161, 12163, 12165, 12167, 12169, 14163, 14165, 14167, 14169, 14195)**: University quarter surrounding Freie Universität Berlin (FU), Schloßstraße retail boulevard.
11. **Reinickendorf (13403, 13405, 13407, 13409, 13435, 13437, 13439, 13465, 13467, 13469)**: Green northern district with light manufacturing and logistics.
12. **Marzahn-Hellersdorf (12619, 12621, 12623, 12627, 12629, 12679, 12681, 12683, 12685, 12687, 12689)**: Open parks (Gärten der Welt), affordable housing opportunities, and healthcare centers.

## 6. Pricing & Employer Services

- **Free for Seekers**: Job seekers and room seekers pay €0. No registration fee, no paywalls.
- **Standard Job Listing**: €29 (30 days active on map, category, and search).
- **Premium Job Listing**: €49 (60 days active, top placement, highlighted badge).
- **Standard Housing Listing**: €29 (30 days active).
- **Premium Housing Listing**: €49 (60 days active, featured tag).
- **Annual Employer Pass**: €499/year (Unlimited job postings, priority indexing, verified badge).
